title: 和 / 也 / 都
explanation: 和  connects nouns ("and"); 也  means "also/too" and sits before the verb; 都  means "all/both" and also sits before the verb, referring to the subject.
structure: Noun + 和 + Noun / Subj + 也 / 都 + Verb

examples.pinyin: wǒ hé tā shì péng yǒu
wǒ yě xǐ huan hē chá
examples.english: I also like to drink tea.

examples.pinyin: wǒ men dōu qù guo shàng hǎi
examples.english: We have both been to Shanghai.

examples.pinyin: píng guǒ hé xiāng jiāo dōu hǎo chī
examples.english: Both apples and bananas are delicious.

notes: 和 only links nouns, never verbs or clauses (use 也/并/而且 for those). 也 and 都 go after the subject and before the verb/auxiliary.
